text:
mike: Heads up — saw repeated GPU node churn in eu-west this morning. CA is killing nodes with warm KV caches and long-running low-latency jobs are spiking. Anyone else seeing this?
priya: Looking now. Do you have the autoscaler flags/config for the cluster?
mike: Yep, grabbed from the control plane. Config looks aggressive: 
```
--expander=least-waste 
--scale-down-unneeded-time=5m 
--scale-down-stable-window=10m 
--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5 
--scale-down-unready-time=5m 
--max-empty-bulk-delete=10
```
Seems tuned for cost, not warm-pool preservation.
anya: Ouch. That unneeded-time is pretty low for GPU workloads — warm caches + model load times mean we want nodes around longer. Suggest bumping `--scale-down-unneeded-time` to 20m and `--scale-down-stable-window` to 30m for the GPU nodegroups. Also consider `--max-empty-bulk-delete=1` to avoid large simultaneous evictions.
javier: Also: are GPU pods using proper priorityClass and PDBs? CA treats pods without a PDB as safe to remove. Some of our latency-sensitive runners don't have PDBs and are marked non-critical, so they get evicted.
priya: Good call. On checking the pod specs for the batch-rt group, I see no PDBs and priorityClass is `standard`. We should create a small PDB (minAvailable: 1) and a `high-priority` class for the model-worker jobs.
mike: There's another wrinkle — network flaps made some nodes briefly NotReady this morning (CNI issues). CA's `--scale-down-unready-time` is 5m so nodes were marked drainable quickly after transient NotReady. Maybe increase that to 15m so transient flaps don't trigger scale-down.
ops-oncall: For GPU pools we also have the option of a warm-pool nodegroup with a taint `warm-pool=true:NoSchedule` and short-lived instances tolerate it. Then we can mark warm nodes as non-evictable by not scheduling other workloads on them. Or add annotation on nodegroup to prevent CA from deleting (`cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled=true`) during peak windows.
javier: If we add taints, remember to add tolerations to the pods that legitimately belong there. Example toleration snippet: 
```yaml
 tolerations:
   - key: "warm-pool"
     operator: "Equal"
     value: "true"
     effect: "NoSchedule"
```
priya: Another small flag tweak: lower `--max-empty-bulk-delete` and raise `--max-node-provision-time` so CA waits longer for preemptible spot allocations instead of immediately killing other nodes to meet binpack goals.
anya: Regarding expanders: `least-waste` is fine for cost but can scatter GPU pods across nodegroups and increase churn. For predictable behavior prefer `priority` or `binpack` for GPU groups — that keeps GPUs consolidated and reduces node churn. We could set per-nodegroup expander preference by using node-group priorities in our autoscaler config.
mike: Action items I hear: 1) bump unneeded/unready times for GPU nodegroups; 2) reduce bulk delete to 1; 3) add PDB + priorityClass to model-worker pods; 4) consider warm-pool taint pattern or annotate nodegroup to temporarily disable scale-down during peak windows; 5) test expander change in staging (binpack/priority).
ops-oncall: I'll open a short runbook and apply conservative CA flags for eu-west GPU groups during the 10:00–14:00 window. Will also add a Grafana alert on `gpu_pod_restart_rate` and `model_latency_p50`.
sre-bot: Deploy started: updating CA flags for cluster eu-west (PR #2289) — applying `--scale-down-unneeded-time=20m`, `--scale-down-stable-window=30m`, `--scale-down-unready-time=15m`, `--max-empty-bulk-delete=1` to gpu nodegroups.
priya: Great, can we also schedule a canary with expander=binpack in staging to measure scale-up/pack efficiency?
anya: I'll run a 4-hour canary this afternoon and post results. If churn drops and tail latency improves, we flip in prod next week.
mike: Thanks all. Please monitor the latency dashboards and post if anything regresses. Will follow up after canary. :thumbsup:
